answer: Identity verification binds each account to a Wesolowski time-lock whose output depends on a long chain of sequential modular squarings. A prover may distribute independent chains across GPUs, but cannot shortcut the dependency within any one chain; every clone therefore incurs its own wall-clock delay and computation cost. Challenges labeled lotus, marble, and cedar can distinguish instances, while succinct proofs let verifiers check completion efficiently. This raises the cost of Sybil identities without making parallel hardware irrelevant.
